title: A retired Airtable key value presented in a bearer header or with no carrier
summary: A synthetic value after Bearer in an Authorization header and a synthetic value alone in prose, both of the kind a retired user API key might take.
rationale: Whether a retired key was also sent in an Authorization bearer header, and what shape it had, is not established by a dated, pinned page: the current page names only the api_key URL parameter and the archived notice states dates and scope but no format. A pinned capture of the pre-2023 API reference would settle the presentation form. The open question is whether these inputs belong to this family; it says nothing about how a bearer header value or a bare token in general is handled, which other families and generic Cases decide.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for this family: the presentation form of the retired key (URL parameter, bearer header or both) and its format are not stated by any pinned page read. A pinned capture of the pre-2023 Airtable API reference, or an Airtable statement of the format, would settle it.

sources.supports: Passing personal access tokens and OAuth access tokens via the legacy api_key URL parameter is not supported; the page names api_key as the URL parameter of the former key mechanism and does not describe the former key's format.
The archived notice states dates and the all-or-nothing scope of the API key but no prefix, alphabet, length or presentation form.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. No outcome is asserted: the open question named in the expectation is what would have to be settled first.
